page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B14 processors, providing 90 vCPUs across 45 physical cores with two threads per core. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16) alongside AES and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Memory allocation totals 360 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is integrated directly via 3216 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across eight drives, while hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmarking results reflect high computational capacity across parallel workloads. The server achieves top-tier results in Clang software compilation, PassMark CPU tests, and extended instruction execution, as well as ray tracing benchmarks. Multi-threaded processing scores in Stress-NG and Geekbench place within the top quartile. Memory subsystem performance shows fast read throughput of 6372.53 GB/sec for cached blocks and 217.44 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, paired with an average large-block write rate of 76.89 GB/sec. Operational throughput is reinforced by database test results of 30,061.14 operations per second in PassMark and 117.73 million Redis SET operations per second.

The dense core count and bundled high-speed NVMe storage deliver strong resource efficiency for IOPS-sensitive applications without requiring external disk attachments. A balanced compute-to-memory architecture suits large-scale software builds, relational and non-relational database management systems, static web infrastructure, and high-concurrency microservices. However, lack of included public IPv4 addresses requires additional network planning, and single-threaded performance remains moderate relative to its multi-core capabilities.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90-lssd is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 90 vCPUs and 45 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, running on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 360 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 3216 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage across eight drives. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-decile performance in Clang software compilation and PassMark CPU extended instruction execution, alongside strong results in multi-core compute, Redis transactions exceeding 117 million operations per second, and database operations. The server does not include dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addressing. The configuration offers efficient resource density for multi-threaded, I/O-intensive workloads such as large-scale build automation, high-throughput caching layers, enterprise database hosting, and web serving clusters.
